creator.name: Agesander, Athenodoros and Polydorus of Rhodes

object.description: The priest of Troy who warned against the wooden horse, and the sea serpents sent to silence him, dying with his sons. Pliny saw it in the palace of Titus and called it the finest work of art in the world; it was dug up in a vineyard on the Esquiline on 14 January 1506, Michelangelo went to watch, and the Pope bought it within a month. Its agony taught the Renaissance and the Baroque what a body could express, Lessing wrote the founding essay of modern aesthetics about why its mouth is not screaming, and Bernini and Blake and Goethe all took it as the measure. This is a cast of the Vatican marble; the arm bent back over the head is the right one, found in 1906, replacing the straight arm the Renaissance had guessed.
facts: Michelangelo refused to restore it, saying no one could; Montorsoli's straight arm stood until 1957.
Napoleon took it to Paris in 1798; it came back in 1816.
Lessing's 'Laocoön' (1766) argues that sculpture must choose the moment before the climax, not the climax.
